cpa_enactment.child_handles: bundles of ten sticks (a ten) and single loose sticks (a one); ten bundles taped together make one big hundred-bundle
cpa_enactment.quantity_visible: the actual bundles and sticks laid out in Hundreds/Tens/Ones columns, one drawn/handled item per unit -- never a bare digit alone

concrete_model.name: bundles of ten sticks (a ten), and ten bundles taped together into one big bundle (a hundred)
concrete_model.ten: one bundle = ten sticks tied with a rubber band
concrete_model.free_source: ice-lolly sticks, broom sticks or dry twigs the class gathers from the yard; rubber bands from a shop bundle -- the teacher ties enough bundles once and reuses them all year

boardWork.instruction: Before class, draw a 3-column Hundreds | Tens | Ones chart on the board. Draw bundles and sticks for each example -- never write a bare digit alone.

steps.action: Draw/lay out 1 hundred-bundle, 2 ten-bundles and 3 loose sticks in the H/T/O chart for 123 (p.3's own example). Count each column aloud before writing any digit.
steps.say: Look: one big bundle of a hundred, two bundles of ten, three loose sticks. That is 1 hundred, 2 tens, 3 ones -- we write 123. In expanded form: 100 + 20 + 3.

cfu.question: What is the value of the digit 2 in 123?
cfu.pass_signal: Says 20, pointing to the two ten-bundles (2 tens = 20), not just 'it's a 2'.
cfu.if_struggle: Cover the digit 2 with your hand and ask: how many ten-bundles are still there? Count them: 2 bundles = 20.

steps.action: Together, help Zainab build 256 with bundles: 2 hundred-bundles, 5 ten-bundles, 6 loose sticks. Fill the H/T/O chart together, counting each column before writing.
steps.say: How many hundred-bundles does Zainab need for 256? Two. Tens? Five bundles. Ones? Six sticks. Let's write the expanded form together: 200 + 50 + 6.

cfu.question: Which digit in 256 tells us the TENS, and what is its value?
cfu.pass_signal: Points to the 5 and says tens place, value 50 (not just 5).

steps.action: Independently complete p.4's Practice Questions on 602: the H/T/O blanks, expanded form, each digit's place and value, and count backward/forward.
steps.say: Now build 602 on your own. Remember: an empty tens column still gets a 0 written down.

cfu.question: Why does 602 have NO ten-bundles at all?
cfu.pass_signal: Says the tens digit is 0, so zero bundles of ten are needed, and the tens column stays empty.

generated.workedExample: 342 (the book's own second worked example, p.3-4). Draw 3 hundred-bundles, 4 ten-bundles and 2 loose sticks FIRST, then write the notation: 342 = 300 + 40 + 2. The digit 3 is in the hundreds place, value 300; digit 4 is in the tens place, value 40; digit 2 is in the ones place, value 2. (A different number from the 123 used in I-Do and the 256 used in We-Do.)

partnerActivity.structure: Digit Detective (anxiety-safe, no timer, 3-5 min): Partner A names a 3-digit number, Partner B says its hundreds/tens/ones digits and their values; swap. Each child tracks only their OWN correct-in-a-row streak, never compared to a classmate.
partnerActivity.dialogueFrameA: My number is ___. What are its hundreds, tens and ones?
partnerActivity.teacher_role: circulate, listening for VALUE not just digit-naming (e.g. 'tens = 40', not just 'tens = 4'); reset a pair's streak with encouragement, never a penalty.

problems.solution: 6 hundreds, 0 tens, 2 ones (p.4, confirmed by the 6 hundred-bundles / empty tens column / 2 sticks picture).

problems.prompt: The digit 6 in 602 is in ___ place. The digit 0 is in ___ place. The digit 2 is in ___ place.
problems.solution: 6 = hundreds place; 0 = tens place; 2 = ones place (p.4).

problems.prompt: The value of 6 in 602 is ___. The value of 0 is ___. The value of 2 is ___.
Count backwards from 602: ___, ___, ___, 598. Count forward from 602: ___, ___, ___, 606.

generated.weakLearnerSupport: Named strategy: Bundle-Count-First. The struggling student physically lays out the bundles and sticks into the H/T/O chart BEFORE writing any digit, counts each column aloud, and only then writes the digit that matches the count -- never writes a digit first and justifies it afterward.
generated.challengeExtension: Ahead learners (Ayesha's group) take a number with a REPEATED digit, like 232, and explain out loud why the two '2's are worth different amounts (200 vs 2) even though they look the same.

exitTicket.task: Ahmed says 470 (4 hundreds + 7 tens + 0 ones) is the SAME number as 407 (4 hundreds + 0 tens + 7 ones). Is he right? Explain using place value.
exitTicket.success_criteria: Correct if the student says DIFFERENT and explains that the 7 and 0 sit in different places (tens vs ones), so they are worth different amounts (70 vs 7).
exitTicket.self_prediction: Before answering, draw ☺ or ☹ predicting whether 470 and 407 will turn out to be the same number.

generated.homework: Bilal has the number 385: write how many hundreds, tens and ones, write it in expanded form, then count forward 3 numbers from it.
generated.keyFact: The SAME digit is worth a different amount depending on which place it sits in -- hundreds, tens, or ones.
generated.cfuExplain: If a student names the digit instead of its value (says '2' instead of '20'), ask them to count the bundles in that column out loud before answering again.
generated.coachingReflection: Notice whether children can state a digit's VALUE (not just its name) without being prompted to count the bundles first.
generated.nextTopicPreview: Next lesson learns how to say and write the NAMES of these 3-digit numbers in words.

misconception (named for the AUTHOR stage): children read a digit's NAME as its VALUE -- saying '2' for the tens digit in 123 instead of '20'. Because both '342' and '256' place a digit in the tens column, this is why the value is asked explicitly at every surface, not just the digit's name.
